examples.name: Default
examples.summary: An official diagram picked by `name`: the AI Gateway cost routing. It carries its own description, so it needs no `aria-label`. Switch `name` in Controls to see every registered diagram.

examples.name: Spec
examples.summary: A one-off diagram passed as `spec`. The request path of a workload. The workload is the one `lit` node, the path the request takes is `active` on its nodes and edges, and the row is `wide` so the `hit` and `miss` chips have room. Narrow the canvas and the row stacks, the branches indent under the workload, and the connectors follow.

examples.name: NodeKinds
examples.summary: One node of each kind: `app`, the quiet window of the consumer application; `pill`, the client; `card`, a platform piece with its eyebrow, icon and status; `item`, a model or provider with a mono line under its title; and `tile`, an icon-only cell whose name shows on hover.

examples.name: Groups
examples.summary: Groups frame part of the layout under a small label, and edges can reach a group as a whole. The platform group holds a `grid` of tiles; the backend group is `dashed` and tinted with the secondary mask to mark it as outside the platform.

examples.name: Flow
examples.summary: A vertical flow in a docs column: one `row` that stacks below the wide breakpoint. The nodes sit centred on one axis, each connector runs from the bottom centre of a node to the top centre of the next, and the `azion deploy` chip sits centred on its line.
